title: Robustness: The Results Without the First-Deal Restriction
guards_added: FEATURE, not swap: first-deal stays the conservative MAIN spec (one clean event per firm, no overlapping within-firm windows); the all-deals-stacked panels and the two binary logits are the robustness that survives. NEVER propose all-deals-as-main.

These six objects ANSWER the first-deal threat disclosed at 2.4 P5.2 ('only the FIRST deal sets the event clock ... first-deal focus remain assumptions, not identification') -- frame them as the answer to that disclosed threat, not as a fresh result.

No-redundancy: cite ONLY the all-deals-stacked panel of each robustness table; the first-deal panel == the existing main table (tab:empire_building_did / tab:empire_drop_matched / tab:empire_drop_placebo / tab:empire_cashspec) and is NEVER restated. The two logits (A, B) have NO fixed effects (pooled cross-section; firm-FE infeasible at the base rate) -> DIRECTION-consistent with, not equivalent to, the within-firm main. Logit A pools ALL payment types -> backs the GENERAL run-up only and CANNOT separate cash from stock (that separation is Logit B). Logit B's stock arm is underpowered (N=123, 88.9% cash base rate).

The all-deals stock Drop PRE1-GAP -0.0585* is SIGNIFICANT but NEGATIVE -> stock moves the OPPOSITE way (cf. the first-deal stock arm at 3.4-PARA1-a, same direction); it is NOT a crack in the stock flat null. The first-deal stock number itself is held for the framing-TODO (one-main-coefficient rule).

The formal cash-concentration EFFECT is stronger all-deals (Wald 0.1056** vs 0.0983**) but the proposed CAUSE stays n.s. (0.0071) -> war-chest mechanism OPEN; concentration, NOT strict specificity ('we interpret, we do not detect').
